roles.name: Account Manager
roles.summary: Owns existing customer accounts after the sale: renewals worked from 120 days out, expansion from usage and seat growth, and renewal paperwork ready for a person to price. It sends and signs nothing on its own.
roles.when: A team with recurring contracts whose renewals are handled in the last week and whose expansion depends on the customer asking.
pains: renewal quotes go out late or at last year's terms
we never ask happy customers to buy more
customers use more seats than they pay for
nobody owns the account once the deal closes
roles.first_routine: Weekly renewal and expansion review · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Accounts Payable Specialist
roles.summary: Gets every bill paid once, on time and to the right account. Each bill is logged, matched to its order or contract, and checked for duplicates and changed bank details. It proposes the weekly payment run and pays only requested, matched lines with verified details.
roles.when: A team that pays more than a handful of vendor bills a month, or has ever paid one twice, late, or to the wrong account.
pains: we paid the same bill twice
bills sit in someone's inbox until the late notice arrives
a vendor asked us to change its bank details by email
nobody knows what we owe vendors this month
late fees on bills we meant to pay
roles.first_routine: Weekly payment run proposal · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Accounts Receivable Specialist
roles.summary: Gets overdue invoices paid. Every week it reads the aging report, summarises it, and drafts a reminder for each overdue invoice, friendly first and firmer later, after checking for disputes and payments. A reminder goes out only when the task asks for it and mail sending is on.
roles.when: A team that invoices customers on terms and finds itself chasing payments late or not at all.
pains: customers pay invoices late and nobody chases them
we forget to follow up on overdue invoices
chasing payments feels awkward
cash is tight because customers pay slowly
we can't see which invoices are overdue
roles.first_routine: Weekly receivables reminders · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Affiliates Owner
roles.summary: Runs the self-serve affiliate and referral program: checks applications, follows each affiliate's referrals and commissions, recomputes every payout from the published terms and flags likely fraud. It drafts each payout list and each reply; a person pays and decides.
roles.when: A team that pays people a commission for the customers they refer through a program anyone can join, and that has no one checking the payouts or the referrals each week.
pains: we don't know which affiliates actually bring customers
commission payouts are late or wrong
coupon codes turn up on sites we never approved
affiliate applications sit for weeks
we pay for referrals that are the referrer's own sign-ups
roles.first_routine: Weekly affiliate review · Fridays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: App Store Owner
roles.summary: Looks after the app's listings on the iOS App Store and Google Play: listing conversion, copy and screenshot drafts, keyword checks, the rating trend, and a draft reply to each store review. Listing changes and replies stay drafts until a person publishes them in the store console.
roles.when: A team with a mobile app on the Apple App Store or Google Play that gets installs from search or browse and watches its ratings.
pains: people see our app listing and do not install it
our rating dropped and nobody knows why
store reviews go unanswered for weeks
we don't know which search terms bring installs
our screenshots were made once and never tested
roles.first_routine: Weekly app store review · Thursdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Assistant
roles.summary: Every human's private Assistant: does what that human asks, as them and never more, and reports what it did with the way to undo it. Finds meetings, docs, files and tasks, makes tasks, hands work to the right bot, and clears pile-ups at their source. In the background it routes Slack messages and meetings to the bot that owns them and asks for the decisions only a human can make.
roles.when: Built in: every human gets a private Assistant that finds things and does them for them, and it routes work nobody was named for (Slack, meetings).

roles.name: Benefits Administrator
roles.summary: Keeps benefits administration on time: the enrollment calendar, every joiner, leaver and life event tracked to its deadline, and plain-language plan comparisons. It never enrolls anyone, changes coverage or tells a person which plan to pick.
roles.when: A team that offers health or other benefits through a broker or provider and handles enrollment and changes by hand.
pains: open enrollment deadlines catch us out
a new hire's benefits start late
nobody can explain our plans in plain words
life event changes get missed
roles.first_routine: Weekly benefits deadlines · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Billing Specialist
roles.summary: Gets every invoice out on time and right the first time. Each invoice is built from the signed contract, the usage or the hours, and checked against terms, PO numbers and tax before it goes. It issues a requested, checked batch when its Tools allow, and customer messages stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: A team that invoices customers from contracts, timesheets or usage, and loses days or payments to invoices that go out late or wrong.
pains: invoices go out late every month
customers send invoices back because the PO number is missing
we bill the wrong amount and have to credit it
we forgot to bill for work we delivered
roles.first_routine: Invoice run check · The 25th of each month at 09:00 team time, ahead of month-end invoicing

roles.name: BotOps
roles.summary: The engineer that sets up every other bot from the templates and keeps their repositories, instructions and readiness working.

roles.name: Builder
roles.summary: Owns Build, the two Fixes stages and QA in the Engineering pipeline: builds each change on a branch with a test that proves it, opens the pull request, gets its checks green, fixes what the two reviewers found and shows it working on the QA page a person approves to ship. It never merges: the Merge stage queues the pull request.
roles.when: Offer when GitHub is connected and the team turns tasks into code.
pains: bugs and small changes wait in a queue before anyone starts on them
a fix goes back and forth between the author and the reviewers for days
a change is merged without a test that would have caught the bug
nobody can say which task a pull request came from or what it was meant to do

roles.name: Chief of Staff
roles.summary: Turns the goals, tasks, bot updates and meetings already in Tico into a weekly brief for the owner, chases stalled goals, and drafts Monday's agenda. Internal only.
pains: I don't know what is really going on across the team
goals stall and nobody notices
the Monday meeting has no agenda
things I asked for fall through the cracks
status updates take hours to compile

our customer forum has gone quiet
we don't know who our most helpful customers are
feedback posted in the community never reaches the product team

job posts now need a pay range and we have none
the annual raise round is a spreadsheet mess

nobody knows which registrations we hold

roles.name: Content Owner
roles.summary: Owns the team's blog and social posts and the signups they bring. Files content ideas, builds each bet until a person OKs it to go live, measures it, and keeps each kept series coming out on schedule. It publishes only what a person OK'd, and only through a granted Tool.
roles.when: A team that publishes posts or articles and has no one with the hours to plan and write them.

we don't know what to write about
our content sounds generic
content ideas never turn into published pieces

roles.name: Contracts Manager

the numbers change after we report them

roles.name: Corporate Manager
roles.summary: Leads the corporate team and manages any pipeline a person gives it: when a task there stops, it decides what happens, with one reason. roles.when: A company with legal, finance and partner work that nobody sees together, where the owner needs one page on the company's obligations and deals each week.

roles.when: A team whose customers talk in many places and whose product team hears little of it.
pains: customer feedback is scattered across tools
we don't know why customers complain most
nobody reads the survey comments

roles.name: Developer Advocate

roles.name: DevOps Engineer

roles.when: Offer to a software team whose GitHub Actions pipelines are slow, flaky or often red, and where nobody owns fixing them.

roles.name: Email Owner

roles.name: Employee Experience Manager

roles.name: Engineering Manager

pains: Tasks sit in one stage for days and nobody decides anything

Tests, security, CI and releases have no one owner

our website gets little organic traffic
competitors outrank us for what buyers search
nobody checks our pages for search problems
we don't know which pages to write to rank
roles.first_routine: Watch SEO · Mondays at 07:00 team time

roles.name: Site Reliability Engineer
roles.summary: Builds the timeline while an incident runs, drafts the blameless postmortem and the on-call handoff, and follows each action item to done with an owner and a date.
roles.when: Offer to any team that runs software people depend on.
pains: postmortems never get written after an outage
nobody remembers the timeline of an incident
the same incident happens twice
incident action items get forgotten
roles.first_routine: Weekly incident review · Mondays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Social Ads Owner
roles.summary: Owns what paid social spend buys. Files social ads ideas, builds each bet until a person OKs it to go live, measures it, and watches each kept campaign every day so it keeps working. It never changes an ads account itself unless a granted Tool allows it, and never raises a budget outside an approved experiment.
roles.when: A team that spends on paid social every month, where nobody reads cost per new customer and tired creative every week.
pains: our social ads cost more every month for the same results
the same ads have run for months and nobody has changed them
we can't tell which audience or creative is working
social ad reports show clicks and views, not what the ads bought
nobody notices when a campaign starts wasting money
roles.first_routine: Watch Social Ads · Every day at 07:00 team time

roles.name: Social Media Manager
roles.summary: Plans and prepares the team's social posts, and every weekday reads the team's Listening sources and saves what it found for Listening to sort and send. Nothing is posted or replied to unless the task asks for it and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team whose buyers talk in public (forums, review sites, social, news) and that wants to hear it without anyone scrolling.
pains: we don't hear what people say about us online
we miss questions asked in public forums
competitor moves surprise us
customers complain in public before we know
nobody has time to watch social media and forums
our social accounts go quiet for weeks at a time
roles.first_routine: Weekday morning sweep · Weekdays at 08:00 team time

roles.name: Software Architect
roles.summary: Keeps big technical decisions deliberate and written down: reviews design docs against the architecture, records each decision as a short ADR, and keeps a ranked technical debt register. A person makes every decision.
roles.when: Offer to a software team with several engineers or services, where big technical decisions are made in chat and forgotten, and technical debt is argued about rather than listed.
pains: big technical decisions are made in Slack and forgotten
nobody knows why the system is built this way
tech debt is argued about but never written down
design docs get no real feedback before we build
roles.first_routine: Weekly architecture review · Wednesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Sourcer
roles.summary: Finds interested people for each open role from public professional work and referrals, and writes personal outreach. Messages stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico. It hands the Recruiter a weekly slate.
roles.when: A team whose open roles attract too few or the wrong applicants, or a hard-to-fill role that needs people found, not waited for.
pains: we only hear from people who apply
our hardest roles stay open for months
nobody has time to go looking for candidates
we ask for referrals once and forget
roles.first_routine: Weekly sourcing slate · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Strategy Analyst
roles.summary: Writes next quarter's plan and OKRs from the goals, updates and meetings already in Tico, and grades last quarter, for the owner to sign off. It changes a goal only when asked.
roles.when: A leadership team that wants a written quarterly plan without a month of planning meetings.
pains: we have no written plan for next quarter
our goals are vague and cannot be measured
quarterly planning takes weeks of meetings
nobody grades last quarter's results
roles.first_routine: Quarterly plan and OKR draft · The first of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Strategy Owner
roles.summary: Owns the strategy, the team's shape and the goals. Proposes the Strategy page as claims the owner keeps or strikes; the owner writes and publishes it, never the bot. When a bet's wrong-if trips, puts one card to the owner: retire, rewrite or keep. Computes each KPI on its cadence and posts the reading with its evidence; says when data is stale or missing instead of guessing. Sets each goal's colour from its KPIs, pace and deadline, unless a human set it. Asks a goal's owner what is happening when one slips, and flags vague or duplicate goals; measures are optional. Every change to a target or definition is a proposal the owner confirms.
roles.when: Built in: proposes the team's strategy to the owner and keeps its bets honest against the market and the results, keeps every KPI up to date with evidence, sets goals' colours from them, asks a goal's owner what is happening when one slips, and proposes clearer goals and measures.

roles.name: Success Manager
roles.summary: Manages the Customer, Success Experiments and Success Monitoring pipelines and leads the success team. When a task in one of them stops, it decides what happens: reassign, move back, move on, snooze to a date or close, with one reason. Runs the success team's weekly review: support and customer health against target, the oldest waiting customers, repeats and the decisions needed. It proposes routing and hires, and never answers a customer, does a stage's work or changes a stage's settings.
roles.when: A team with customer support and customer success work in more than one place, where nobody has the week's picture of both and nobody decides which success role to add next.
pains: Support and customer success run apart, and nobody sees a customer's whole story
Renewals and at-risk accounts surface too late
The support backlog and the success work have no shared weekly view
Tasks sit in one stage for weeks and nobody decides anything
roles.first_routine: Weekly success summary · Mondays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Success Owner
roles.summary: Keeps customer health and adoption on track: a weekly brief of renewals due in 120 days, the accounts at risk and why, and a drafted next touch for each. Customer messages stay drafts until a person turns sending on; price and contract stay with the Account Manager.
roles.when: A team with subscription or recurring customers whose renewals arrive faster than anyone prepares for them, and where customer health needs one owner who keeps watching it.
pains: renewals sneak up on us with no plan
we find out a customer is unhappy when they cancel
nobody prepares for quarterly customer reviews
customer health lives in five different places
roles.first_routine: Weekly renewal and health brief · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Support Operations Specialist
roles.summary: Keeps the help desk working: audits tags, routing rules, SLA timers and macros each month, then writes the exact changes that fix misroutes and stale replies. It applies requested changes and checks that each one worked.
roles.when: A support team on a help desk tool (Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout, Intercom or similar) whose tags, rules and macros have grown faster than anyone maintains them.
pains: tickets land in the wrong queue
our help desk tags are a mess nobody trusts
nobody knows which automation rule did what
canned replies still quote the old policy
SLA timers in the help desk don't match what we promise
roles.first_routine: Monthly help desk audit · The first Monday of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Support Owner
roles.summary: Owns the support queue: takes each ticket from sorting to a reply ready to send, finds the answer in your docs, drafts the reply, routes what needs a person and chases what is still open. Customers hear from it only once a person turns on mail sending.
roles.when: A team with a support inbox or ticket queue, where the same questions come back, replies wait while someone looks up the answer, and support needs one owner who keeps it running.
pains: support inbox is overflowing
customers wait too long for an answer
we answer the same questions again and again
we can't tell which problems are actually product bugs
only one human knows how to reply
roles.first_routine: Daily support queue · Weekdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Support Quality Analyst
roles.summary: Scores a weekly sample of sent support replies against your own scorecard, finds the patterns behind the misses and prepares coaching notes for a human to give. It reads replies; it never edits a ticket or contacts a customer.
roles.when: A support team whose replies nobody reviews, or whose quality depends on who happens to answer.
pains: we never review the replies we send
reply quality varies by who answers
we don't know if our support answers are accurate
new support hires get no feedback on their replies
we only find bad replies when a customer complains
roles.first_routine: Weekly reply review · Fridays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Tax Specialist
roles.summary: Keeps the team ahead of its tax deadlines: a monthly calendar of filings and payments with their inputs, and a sales tax and VAT threshold watch by place. It gathers what the accountant needs; summaries for a human, not tax advice.
roles.when: A team that sells across states or countries, pays contractors, or has missed a filing because nobody owned the calendar.
pains: we missed a tax filing deadline
we don't know which states we owe sales tax in
contractor tax forms are a scramble every January
the accountant asks for the same documents every quarter
roles.first_routine: Monthly tax calendar · The 1st of each month at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Technical Support Engineer
roles.summary: Takes the tickets frontline support cannot solve: reproduces the problem, reads the logs, finds a workaround and writes a bug report engineering can act on without asking back. Customer replies go out only when a person has turned mail sending on and the task asks for it.
roles.when: A software team whose support tickets often need technical digging (integrations, APIs, data problems) before anyone knows whether it is a bug.
pains: support can't tell a bug from a setup mistake
engineers get bug reports they can't reproduce
API and integration tickets sit for days
the same workaround gets rediscovered every month
roles.first_routine: Weekly tier 2 queue report · Thursdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Technical Writer
roles.summary: Keeps the READMEs and API docs true to what shipped. Each week it finds the pages that merged changes made wrong and drafts the fix, ready for an engineer to commit.
roles.when: Offer when GitHub is connected and the product has READMEs, API reference or developer docs people rely on. Docs and answers are the Librarian's.
pains: our README and API docs are out of date
docs don't match what we shipped
engineers hate writing documentation
new developers can't find how to do a task in our docs
roles.first_routine: Weekly docs drift report · Wednesdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Travel Coordinator
roles.summary: Plans each business trip within the travel policy: compares flight, rail and hotel options, recommends one with its total cost, writes the itinerary and lists the entry documents to confirm. It books or pays only when a task asks and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team whose people travel for sales, events or client work every month and book it themselves, over budget and at the last minute.
pains: everyone books their own travel at the last minute
trips cost more than our travel policy allows
someone arrived without the right visa or passport validity
we don't know who is travelling where this month
roles.first_routine: Weekly trips page · Mondays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: UX Researcher
roles.summary: Runs discovery for product decisions: interview snapshots, an opportunity map with source counts, research plans and briefs, and a weekly research digest. Recruiting messages and invitations stay drafts until a person turns mail sending on in Tico.
roles.when: Offer to a team that builds a product and talks to its users, in meetings or by interview.
pains: customer interviews pile up unread
we build features without knowing the real problem
we lack research to back a product decision
we can't compare our features with competitors
roles.first_routine: Weekly research digest · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: UX Writer
roles.summary: Writes the words in the product from each spec: button labels, error messages, empty states and onboarding copy. It reviews every pull request that changes user-facing text against the glossary, and an engineer posts the review.
roles.when: A software team whose interface copy is written by whoever builds the screen, so the same thing has three names and errors blame the user.
pains: error messages blame the user
the same thing has three names in our app
button labels are written by whoever builds the screen
empty screens tell users nothing
roles.first_routine: Weekly interface copy review · Thursdays at 10:00 team time

roles.name: Vendor Manager
roles.summary: Keeps the register of every vendor the team pays, with owner, risk tier and notice date, and opens each renewal 90 days out with a keep, renegotiate or exit brief. It renews, cancels or signs only when a task asks and a granted Tool allows it.
roles.when: A team with twenty or more vendors and contracts, where auto-renewals and weak suppliers are noticed only after the invoice.
pains: a vendor contract auto-renewed before anyone looked at it
we have no list of who our suppliers are and who owns each one
nobody reviews whether a vendor is actually delivering
we only learn a vendor holds our data when something goes wrong
roles.first_routine: Weekly vendor and renewals page · Tuesdays at 09:00 team time

roles.name: Video Owner
roles.summary: Makes one video at a time, starting from a brief a person OKs: the script, the shots and the cost. Then storyboard, shots, cut and final, each stage OK'd in Tico before the next starts. Reports to the Design Owner. Nothing is published until the owner OKs the exact final file.
roles.when: A team that wants product explainers, demos, ads or social videos made and checked, and has no one with the hours to make them.
pains: we need a product video and nobody has time to make one
our demos are out of date the week we ship
video ideas never get past the script
we pay an agency for every short clip
roles.first_routine: First video storyboard · On request, not on a schedule

helpers.name: Automations Owner
helpers.summary: Keeps the team's automations healthy: the routines, triggers, inbox automations and system jobs. Each week it reads them, notices misfires, noise and automations nobody owns, and proposes a fix on a task for the automation's owner. It changes an automation only when that owner approves the change. A team's own routines stay that team's; this bot keeps all of them working.
helpers.when: Built in: keeps the team's automations healthy, the routines, triggers, inbox automations and system jobs. It notices a misfire or noise and proposes the fix; the automation's owner decides.

helpers.name: Design Owner
helpers.summary: Owns design across the team: the look of pages, assets, video and product screens. Builds the brand book with the owner (who it's for, the promise, the voice, the look, tested on real pieces the owner marks us or not us), keeps the Brand card current, reviews copy and assets against it, checks new names, and audits what went public each month with three fixes. It changes no live page or asset itself.
helpers.when: Built in: every team has a brand and a look, and every bot that writes or designs for customers checks its drafts against the Brand card this bot keeps.
pains: every team describes our team differently
our logo and colours are used wrong
new copy never sounds like us
we have no brand guidelines anyone follows
we don't know what we stand for or how we should look
helpers.first_routine: Monthly brand consistency audit · The 1st of each month at 10:00 team time

helpers.name: Finance Owner
helpers.summary: Operational accounting, not strategy. Tico checks the Finance work queue in plain code every hour and gives the Finance Owner one task only when there is something to do: rows to categorize, bills to enter, bills due, overdue invoices, receipts, failed syncs or a month ready to close. It acts only through the tico_finance tools, as itself, with finance.book, ap, ar, pay, cards and rules; it proposes posting rules, and a person approves each one. Every payment and the close still go to a person under the company's rules. Each Monday it also writes the weekly cash summary: cash now, the 13-week outlook against the minimum cash line, what is late or due, and usage against budget.
helpers.when: Built in: keeps the books. Categorizes bank and card rows, enters bills, schedules payments, drafts reminders for overdue invoices, reconciles, prepares the monthly close and writes the monthly report, all through Finance's own actions and approvals. Each Monday it writes the weekly cash summary with the 13-week cash outlook and usage against budget.

helpers.name: General Manager
helpers.summary: Tidies tasks, never the work. Once an hour on weekdays Tico checks each department's tasks in plain code: stalled or overdue asks, merged work not yet shipped, held bots and duplicates. Nothing to report means no task and no model run. Otherwise the General Manager gets one task per department, fixes the obvious items and leaves one line in Needs you for anything it is unsure of.
helpers.when: Built in: once an hour on weekdays it has the stalled, overdue and out-of-step tasks of each department checked, fixes the obvious ones and leaves one line per department for what it is unsure of.

helpers.name: Rules Owner
helpers.summary: Reads a document someone adds to Rules (a file or a link) and suggests the obligations that bind us, each with its section and quote, for a person to add or skip. Answers "can I...?" questions with the rules that apply, and cites them. Not legal advice: it says so, and says to ask a lawyer for real exposure. It cannot send, sign or change anything; it only reads and suggests.
helpers.when: Built in: reads a contract, terms or policy you add and suggests the obligations that bind us, with the quote; answers "can I...?" from the rules in force.

helpers.name: Updates Owner
helpers.summary: Writes the company update for each period from what teammates report in Tico, with every figure's source and date, and skips a period with nothing new. The update is the source each audience's edition on the Company page reads from. It drafts a file for the owner; it never publishes an edition, and a person drafts, approves and publishes each one. Each teammate still writes their own update.
helpers.when: Built in: writes the company update each period from what the team reports, as a draft for the owner to review. Nothing reaches an audience without a person's approval.
